Opening the Files We Send You

Most of what the AI tools produce arrives as one of two file types - an .html report or a .md notes file. Here is how to open each one and see it the way it's meant to look.
For Team Members
STAFF REFERENCE

Two file types cover almost everything we send you. Neither needs special software, and neither sends your file anywhere - both open right on your own computer.

The short version: an .html file is a web page - download it and double-click, or drag it onto a Google Chrome window. A .md file is formatted text - open it in Pinion.md for a clean view, or read it raw in any text editor.
.html - reports and dashboards
Reports, digests, checklists, dashboards. Opens in your browser. Use Chrome.
.md - notes and references
Procedures, notes, reference docs. Readable as-is; nicer in a Markdown reader like Pinion.md.

Part 1 - HTML files (.html)

An HTML file is just a web page saved to your computer. It ends in .html. You don't need internet for it and you don't need any special software - your web browser already opens it.

1
Download the file
Save it somewhere you'll find it again - your Downloads folder or Desktop is fine. If it came as an attachment or a link, choose Download (not "open in a new tab," which may just show the raw code).
2
Double-click it
It should open in your default browser automatically. If it opens as plain code or in the wrong app, right-click the file → Open with → Google Chrome.
3
Read it like a web page
Scroll, click buttons, expand sections - it behaves like any site. Nothing is sent anywhere; the file lives on your computer.

Use Google Chrome. Any browser will open an HTML file - Edge, Firefox, Safari - so if you're in a pinch, use what you have. But we standardize on Google Chrome at School Tech, and some of what we build uses features that only render fully in Chrome.

Heads-up: open our files in Chrome to get the full effect. In Edge or another browser, most of it still works, but you may see missing pieces or things that don't behave the way they should. When something looks broken, re-open it in Chrome before assuming the file is wrong.

To make Chrome your default so double-clicking always uses it: Chrome menu (⋮) → Settings → Default browser → Make default. Or on Windows: Settings → Apps → Default apps and set Chrome for web pages.

It opened as a wall of code. You're seeing the raw HTML, not the page. Right-click the file → Open with → Google Chrome.
It won't open / opens in a text editor. The file is set to open in the wrong app. Right-click → Open with → Choose another app → pick Google Chrome and check "always use this app."
You only see a download link, never the page. Some email and chat tools preview the code instead of rendering it. Download the file first, then open the downloaded copy.

Part 2 - Markdown files (.md)

A Markdown file ends in .md. It's just text with a few simple marks - # for a heading, - for a bullet, **bold** for bold. Open it raw and it's perfectly readable; open it in a Markdown reader and those marks turn into real headings, bullets, and bold text.

Easiest: Pinion.md (no install). Pinion.md is a free in-browser Markdown reader and editor we already use - nothing to install, and it works in Chrome.

1
Open Pinion.md
Go to pinion.buildwithbaker.io - it's also linked at the bottom of the Help Center under the tools we've built.
2
Open or drop in your .md file
Use its open-file option, or drag the .md file onto the page. You can also paste Markdown text straight in.
3
Read the clean version
The # and - marks become real headings and bullets. You can edit and save changes locally too.

Other ways to read a .md file. Use whatever's convenient - any of these work:

Any Markdown reader you like
If you already use a Markdown app or browser extension, keep using it. They all render the same .md format. Pinion.md is just our no-install default.
A plain text editor
Right-click → Open with → Notepad (or any editor). You'll see the raw marks, but .md is written to be readable as-is - fine for a quick look.
Don't double-click expecting a formatted view. On most computers a .md file isn't linked to any app, so double-clicking may do nothing or open raw text. Open it through Pinion.md or your reader of choice instead.
That's it. For an .html file: download → double-click (or drag into Chrome) → read. For a .md file: Pinion.md for a clean read, any text editor for a quick glance. When in doubt, Chrome.
